name: Astraguard — Stellar trust scanner
description: Instant risk verdicts before you sign a Stellar transaction.

host_permissions: Why https://*/* is required — not optional or narrowable:
Astraguard intercepts window.freighterApi.signTransaction BEFORE it reaches the
Freighter wallet extension. The interception must happen in the page's own JS
context (world: MAIN, run_at: document_start) so the hook is in place before
any dApp script runs.
Stellar dApps are deployed on arbitrary, user-chosen domains. Unlike, say, a
bank extension that only needs to run on one known hostname, there is no fixed
allowlist of dApp URLs — new dApps can appear on any HTTPS domain at any time.
Restricting to a curated list would silently fail to protect users on any dApp
not yet on that list, which is worse than the broad permission.
Why not activeTab + optional/runtime-requested permissions instead?
activeTab is granted only on explicit user gesture (clicking the extension icon).
A transaction signing call happens programmatically inside the dApp — by the
time the user clicks sign, the hook must already be installed. activeTab fires
too late and cannot pre-inject at document_start.
Runtime-requested optional permissions (chrome.permissions.request) also
require a user gesture, carry the same timing problem, and would create an
extremely jarring UX: a permission prompt appearing in the middle of a
transaction flow. Users would likely deny it, leaving themselves unprotected.
Conclusion: https://*/* is the minimum permission that makes the protection model
work. This must be declared upfront in the Chrome Web Store listing's permission
justification field (see ARCHITECTURE.md §5 for the exact copy to use).
https://*/*
